parts.note: reads like a useful business acquaintance, but describes the mythical king's gift of turning whatever he touched into gold

explanation.definitionFit: The Phrygian king of legend turned everything he touched to gold, so his touch literally made money; figuratively it is a knack for profit.

definitions.meaning: raised to a higher position or rank

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled after getting a promotion at work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cheered up in spirit and physically or officially raised higher, covering joy and promotion.

clue.text: Protection for king caught in an intriguing situation

indicators.note: the king is trapped inside the love affair, so his letter goes within it

parts.note: an amour is a secret love affair, an intrigue
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A monarch needs protecting after being caught up in some court intrigue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intriguing' looks like political plotting, but here it means a clandestine love affair, AMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour is protective covering worn by soldiers or vehicles, a straightforward synonym for protection.

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is removed, as if beheaded

parts.note: stiff means awkward or stilted in manner

explanation.surface: Someone's head was turned by an awkward quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head put off' removes the first letter S from STIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, a minor argument between friends or lovers.

clue.text: Time will be on its side

definitions.text: Time will be on its side

parts.words: Time will be on its side
parts.note: sounds like the saying that patience will win, but literally means the hours are shown on the face of a tall building

explanation.definitionFit: A tall structure bearing a clock face on its walls literally has the time displayed on its side.

parts.note: Mona is a woman's name
Lisa is a second woman's name

explanation.surface: A pair of ladies share a grin in unison.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both names; together they form the title of the painting famous for its smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait is renowned for its subject's enigmatic smile, so the painting is one smiling figure.

indicators.note: the letters are organised, arranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Introducing a gay liberation group by name.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a campaign group, but 'organisation' rearranges LIB into BLI, and THE follows; 'gay' is used in its older sense of carefree.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe and gay in its traditional sense both mean cheerful, carefree and light-hearted.

indicators.note: one word hosts the other, holding it inside

parts.note: tar is a traditional slang word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman plays host to the boy of a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsar was the title of the Russian emperor before 1917.

parts.note: contracted to I'm
partial means not complete, only in part

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are not entirely just.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read 'I'm partial', which is the opposite of the definition: a neat contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartial means unbiased and even-handed, which is what being fair means.

clue.text: Looks to be an own goal by Leslie

parts.note: OG is the standard football abbreviation for an own goal
Les is a short form of the name Leslie

explanation.surface: It seems a footballer called Leslie has scored against his own side.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to look at someone with obvious desire, so ogles is a verb form of looks.

clue.text: Substandard may mean a small reduction in price

definitions.meaning: a little discount knocked off the cost

explanation.surface: Inferior goods might be sold at a slight discount.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means slightly wrong or unacceptable, and literally a little amount taken off a price.

clue.text: A novel division of the church

definitions.meaning: the governing body of canons of a cathedral

explanation.surface: Describing a new split within the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new', but means a book. A cathedral's governing body of clergy is its chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a numbered section of a book and an assembly of cathedral clergy.

clue.text: A paid informer in the private sector?

definitions.text: A paid informer in the private sector?

parts.words: A paid informer in the private sector?
parts.note: suggests a hired spy in business, but means someone paid to give private lessons, informing a pupil

explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher is paid to impart knowledge to individual students outside public schooling.

definitions.meaning: those who retain or keep possession of something
household attendants of a noble family

explanation.surface: Describing employers who have domestic staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means those who retain things and also, traditionally, servants of a great household.

parts.note: looks like sports practice, but the players are actors preparing a show

explanation.definitionFit: Actors practise a play in run-throughs before performing it publicly.

clue.text: Heather undresses without seeing the youths

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: strips means takes clothes off
ling is a common heather plant

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather takes her clothes off unaware of some young men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant LING; 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Striplings are youths, adolescent boys not yet fully grown.

parts.note: a meteorological depression is a low-pressure system, so suffering from it is being beneath bad weather

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means feeling unwell or low, and literally describes being beneath a weather system.

clue.text: Money held in trust not long ago

indicators.note: the money is held within the other word

parts.note: to rely on is to trust
a cent is a small coin of money

explanation.surface: Cash was placed in a trust fund a short while back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trust' looks like a financial trust, but it is the verb RELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, at a time not long past.

indicators.note: a solution is a working-out, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A watertight explanation of how a crime was committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution of' looks like a detective's answer, but signals rearranging THECRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermetic seal is completely airtight, named after Hermes Trismegistus of alchemy.

clue.text: It raises the issue of a senior professorial post

definitions.meaning: a seat that lifts a child, issue meaning offspring

explanation.surface: Something prompts the question of an important university appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raises the issue' looks like bringing up a topic, but issue means children.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a tall seat for feeding infants, and could jokingly mean an elevated professorship.

clue.text: One of the men in a boat helps the pilot

definitions.text: One of the men in a boat
definitions.meaning: one of the three friends in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat
slang name for an aircraft's automatic pilot

explanation.surface: A crew member on a boat assists the navigator.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerome's 1889 novel follows J, Harris and George on the Thames; pilots nicknamed the autopilot 'George'.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a character in the comic novel and is airmen's slang for an autopilot.

explanation.surface: Wreckage left after a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is both discarded waste material and, informally, a fight or scuffle.

clue.text: A sweet's made up in layers

indicators.note: the letters are made up into a new arrangement

parts.note: read as sweets, plural; tarts are sweet pastries

explanation.surface: A dessert is assembled in tiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers of rock or society, so the word stands for things arranged in layers.

indicators.note: one word enters the other and sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
to bound is to spring or leap

explanation.surface: Plants thrive when springtime arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is the verb BOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to be plentiful, to flourish in great numbers.

definitions.meaning: a jar is a harsh jolting shock or grating sound

explanation.surface: A grille stands barely open.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means slightly open, and split into two words gives a harsh jarring noise.

clue.text: Asian playing solitaire, but not having to?

indicators.note: the letters of the card game are played around into a new order

explanation.surface: An Asian person plays patience but doesn't need to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges SOLITAIRE, and 'but not having to' removes T and O, leaving the letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a native of Israel, a country in western Asia.

clue.text: Originator of intrigue in the past

definitions.text: Originator of intrigue in the past

indicators.note: the originator is the starting point, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Describing the person who started a plot long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes Shakespeare's Othello villain, who devised the intrigue.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming villain of Othello, whose plotting drives the tragedy.

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the word is turned back, read right to left

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: A newspaper story recovers backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper; it is the guardian angel. 'back' turns LEG into GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel is believed to watch over and protect a person.

parts.note: sounds like a showy footballer, but means a bolt that flashes and strikes the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A lightning bolt flashes across the sky and strikes, so it is a flashy striker.
